title: Use the internet and apps wisely and safely

say: Use the internet and apps wisely and safely.
This is the video for Module 3 of Smartphone and Digital Awareness: using the internet and helpful apps.
Your phone can do far more than chat. With a browser such as Chrome, you can read news, fill forms and follow an online course.

say: One. A real screen lock, such as a PIN of at least six digits.

say: Two. Install updates. They fix security holes that criminals use.

say: Three. Google Play Protect checks your apps. Most dangerous apps arrive as APK files through WhatsApp links. If your phone asks to install unknown apps, say no.

panel.heading: Six habits that keep your phone safe
items: Back up contacts, photos and WhatsApp
panel.rule: Install apps only from the Play Store. Refuse unknown APK files.

say: Four. Check permissions. Does this app need my contacts, location or SMS to do its job?

say: Five. Switch on Google backup, Google Photos backup and WhatsApp chat backup.

say: Six. Switch on Find My Device, so you can ring, lock or erase a lost phone.

say: For example, Funmi in Ilorin opens Permission manager. A free torchlight app has access to her contacts, location and SMS. A torch needs none of that, and her phone already has a flashlight tile, so she uninstalls it.
WhatsApp needs the microphone for voice notes, but only while she uses it. So she changes it to Allow only while using the app. The whole check took about ten minutes.
The Calculator app is already on your phone and needs no data. For example, Esther in Makurdi checks the trader's bill.

say: Noodles at about 7,500 naira, oil at about 3,200 naira, and seasoning at about 1,800 naira.

card.title: Checking a market bill with the Calculator

say: The total is 12,500 naira. The trader offers 10% off, so she uses the percent button and gets 1,250 naira. She pays 11,250 naira, and counts 3,750 naira change from 15,000 naira.
The history button shows every step she typed, so she knows the numbers are right.

say: Before you install, check the developer is the real company, for example the bank's own name for a bank app. Be wary of a famous name with very few downloads.
Read recent low-star reviews, check the Data safety section, and see if there are ads or payments inside.
And remember, uninstalling an app does not cancel its subscription.
You do not need every platform. Choose one or two that fit what you want. Keep your personal account private, and hide your phone number and address.

panel.heading: Start on social media with care

cards.d: Set personal accounts to private. Hide your phone number and home address from the public.
Fake accounts, scams, harassment. Take screenshots first, then report and block.
Digital Wellbeing shows your screen time. Set app timers and Bedtime mode.

say: If an account is fake, a scam, or harassing you, take screenshots, then use the three dots to report and block.

say: To remember. Bookmark your bank. Keep the six safety habits. Check an app page before you install it.
Keep personal accounts private, and before you post, ask: is it true, and is it mine to share?
